perspective:
Jose Castillo’s available information:

- He works at a community bank and occasionally helps with maintenance/repairs. Patricia Ndiaye is his colleague and a bank teller there; they have a friendly, professional relationship.
- He noticed Patricia seemed more withdrawn/down than usual. He remembers her as vibrant and suspects something is troubling her.
- In their first conversation, he asked if she was okay. Patricia said it was “nothing really,” just “some personal stuff,” and thanked him. He offered to listen; she said she appreciated it.
- During lunch, he overheard Patricia on the phone worrying about bills and financial commitments. This increased his concern.
- He told Patricia he had been reading about financial planning and asked if she’d be interested in discussing it. She said it could be helpful and that she had been overwhelmed with bills. He offered to look over budgeting tips together; she said she’d take him up on it soon.
- He later worried he might have overstepped by bringing up financial planning. He checked with Patricia. She said she didn’t think he was prying and was grateful for his offer. He said he respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend; she said she appreciated it and was glad to have someone to turn to.
- He sensed Patricia appreciated his concern but preferred to handle things privately. He asked about her weekend plans. She said all good, planning a quiet weekend at home. He mentioned reading/relaxing and offered to chat if needed. She thanked him and said she’d keep it in mind.
- He continued checking in supportively at work and offered help with anything, even grabbing coffee. Patricia said she was busy but handling it, thanked him for checking in, said she’d let him know, and that his support was great. He replied anytime and that they all help each other out.

He does not have access to Patricia’s private thoughts, exact financial details, or anything she did not tell him or he did not directly observe/hear.
